You will learn who qualifies for a free ID card, which applications need insurance proof, what form that proof must take, how long insurance documents stay good, and the signed exemption that applies to people who own no registered vehicle, along with the limit it places on them.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Free identification cards","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Homeless with a shelter letter.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02"]},{"text":"Legally blind with a physician letter.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02"]},{"text":"Seventy or older, no extra papers.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"A free identification card is available to three groups with simple proof. An applicant who is homeless brings a letter from a shelter. An applicant who is legally blind brings a letter from a physician. And an applicant seventy or older needs no extra papers at all. Two more situations also qualify. A free ID card is available when your driving record shows a medical cancellation, or when you have a developmental disability documented by a letter from a primary care provider. So the free card follows need, and each group has its own specific proof to bring to the office.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"When insurance proof is required","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"An original license, including transfers.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F03"]},{"text":"A license restored after suspension or revocation.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F03"]},{"text":"A court-granted Limited Driving Privilege.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Insurance proof is required at three moments. A picture of the insurance card on a phone is not accepted, however clear it looks. The insurance certification form, along with insurance binders and certificates, is only good for thirty days after it is issued. A binder from two months ago will not work, even if your policy is still active. That exemption comes with a limit. The driver is restricted to Fleet Vehicles Only, such as company vehicles covered by an employer's fleet policy. Removing the restriction later costs the duplicate fee plus proof of financial responsibility. So the exemption is a real trade: no insurance proof today, but a narrow license until you prove coverage.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s6","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Proof versus exemption","fact_ids":["sec03-R01","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Certification form proves insurance.","fact_ids":["sec03-R01","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-F07"]},{"text":"Exemption means fleet vehicles only.","fact_ids":["sec03-R01","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. So one form proves you are insured, while the other states that you do not need personal coverage and accepts a restriction in return. That search can add time, so plan for it.
